documents.shelfmark: Nationaal Archief 3.01.26, L. P. van de Spiegel, inv. 190

transcription.notes: DECODE's J+ sign stands for different digits; each resolved by a French 6-gram model over the R1024 key values (resolve_j.py).
Three-digit groups include systematic overmarks and undermarks; the supplied HU language tag is erroneous.

system.summary: R1026/R1027 use the 1782 one-part French Grand Chiffre of William V (DECODE key R1024, 1-5000); R1893 uses a distinct three-digit marked-number code.

diacritics.note: R1893 marks individual digits with several overmark/undermark forms; their function is not yet established.

system.sibling_key: DECODE R1024 (Grand Chiffre, KHA A29 inv. 301, 1782) reads R1026/R1027; the control R1028 confirms it.
system.notes: Key entries measured from the R1024 transcription. R1893 remains a separate, unkeyed system.

prior_solution.where: DECODE holds the key (R1024) and plaintext controls R1028/R1029 of the same code; no reading of R1026, R1027 or R1893 was found.

conditions.human_role: The human supplied the task and an existing authenticated DECODE browser cookie.

solution.what: Used the existing private DECODE cookie to download the record metadata, transcriptions, and all seven manuscript images.
Normalized the DECODE J-like glyph as handwritten digit 3 in R1026 and R1027 and extracted numerical groups.
Compared R1026 and R1027 group inventories; they share 49 groups and therefore use the same code system.
Separated R1893 as a different system because its three-digit groups carry systematic per-digit marks absent from the earlier dispatches.
Located Karl de Leeuw's account of Dutch diplomatic code practice and the Nationaal Archief catalogue entry for Van Nagell's 1787 code (current inv. 28).
Downloaded and inspected DECODE R2846 and the interlinearly decrypted control R2243 for related numerical systems.
Decoded the R1028 control (plaintext on DECODE) with key R1024.
Decoded R1026/R1027 with R1024 treating J+ as 3; groups containing J+ read as nonsense.
Resolved each J+ as any digit by beam search with a French 6-gram model (hellen1752 corpus); 105 groups resolved, both letters read.
Assessed R1893 (696 marked three-digit tokens, 513 distinct) for ciphertext-only attack; code too large for the text, no key or crib found.

outcome.method_basis: DECODE's own description names the code as likely William V's 'Grand Chiffre', and that key (R1024, 1782) read R1026 and R1027 once DECODE's catch-all J+ sign was resolved digit by digit with a French 6-gram model; R1028's DECODE plaintext served as control.

gaps.detail: different three-digit overmarked code, 513 distinct forms; keys R2846, R2848, R2850, R2851, R2243 tried; no crib
not in the 1782 R1024 key; 2637/2800/3660 recur, probably names

gaps.item: R1026/R1027 garbled passages from DECODE digit misreads
gaps.detail: NOTES say a fresh transcription from the images would clear them; not done

outcome.notes: R1026 and R1027 read (452 of 472 groups given a value; some passages still garbled by transcription misreads); R1893 not read.
outcome.fraction_read_source: ciphertext_R1026/R1027/R1893.txt (319+152+696 groups) against plaintext_R1026/R1027_raw.txt: groups left as [n?] counted unread (12 in R1026, 8 in R1027; 4 4 3 8 counted read as 4433), all of R1893 unread; 447/1167. Passages garbled by DECODE digit misreads counted as read
